meta.pos: noun; noun; noun; verb; verb; verb

defs.def: a large number of people gathered together in a public place, for example in the streets or at a sports game 人群；观众

ex.s: C her strong urge to follow the crowdD. her dream of entering a top university
ex.t: C 她随大流的强烈冲动D. 她进入顶尖大学的梦想

ex.s: On March 7, 1907, the English statistician Francis Galton published a paper which illustrated what has come to be known as the “wisdom of crowds” effect.
ex.t: 1907年3月7日，英国统计学家弗朗西斯·高尔顿发表了一篇论文，阐述了后来被称为"群体智慧"效应的现象。

ex.s: The key finding of the study was that when crowds were further divided into smaller groups that were allowed to have a discussion, the averages from these groups were more accurate than those from an equal number of independent individuals.
ex.t: 这项研究的关键发现是，当人群被进一步分成可以进行讨论的小组时，这些小组的平均值比同等数量的独立个体的平均值更准确。

ex.s: the crowds were relatively smallB. there were occasional underestimates
ex.t: 人群规模相对较小 B. 偶尔出现低估

ex.s: I quickly searched the crowd for the school’s coach and asked him what had happened.
ex.t: 我迅速在人群中找到学校教练，询问发生了什么事。

ex.s: I quickly searched the crowd for the school's coach and asked him what had happened.
ex.t: 我迅速在人群中找到学校教练，询问发生了什么事。

ex.s: We just follow the crowd.
ex.t: 我们只是随大流。

ex.s: And the crowd desires restful average.
ex.t: 而大众追求安稳平庸。

ex.s: Look how the crowd has gone wild.
ex.t: 看人群多么疯狂。

ex.s: “I’ll see you back home in a month, okay?” His parents nodded, and they watched as he walked out of sight into the crowds of hundreds of students and parents.
ex.t: “一个月后家里见，好吗？”他的父母点点头，看着他消失在数百名学生和家长的人海中。

ex.s: In more technical terms, the wisdom of crowds requires that people’s estimates be independent.
ex.t: 用更专业的术语来说，群体智慧要求人们的估算相互独立。

ex.s: And next time you look up at the sky don’t just look for rain clouds, but also for birds.
ex.t: 下次你仰望天空的时候，不要只寻找雨云，也找找鸟儿吧。

ex.s: When asked why they chose so many AP classes, my friends responded: “I don’t know.” They themselves don’t know why they are following the crowd and longing for the pressures of academic difficulty.
ex.t: 当被问及为什么选择这么多AP课程时，我的朋友们回答说：“我不知道。”他们自己也不知道为什么要随大流，为什么渴望学业压力。

ex.s: It’s lovely at the beach, but not so when you’re wearing a suit and in a crowd of passengers!
ex.t: 在海滩上很好，但当你穿着西装挤在一群乘客中时就不那么好了！

defs.def: a particular group of people 一伙人；一帮人
ordinary people, not special or unusual in any way 群众；民众；老百姓；凡夫俗子
to fill a place so there is little room to move 挤满；塞满；使 … 拥挤

ex.s: French cafés are always crowded.
ex.t: 法国的咖啡馆总是很拥挤。

ex.s: When the stadium is crowded
ex.t: 当体育场拥挤时。

ex.s: Does Kilimanjaro   60   its reputation as a crowded mountain with lines of tourists ruining the atmosphere of peace？I found the opposite to be true.
ex.t: 乞力马扎罗山___60___它作为一座拥挤、游客排成长队破坏宁静氛围的山之名声了吗？我发现事实恰恰相反。

ex.s: Sentences (a) and (b) are from the reading passage.] a Last year, hundreds of people spent good money on an experience that they knew would include crowds, discomfort and danger.
ex.t: （a）（b）两句出自阅读篇章。a 去年，数百人花高价购买了一种他们知道会包含拥挤、不适和危险的体验。

ex.s: After Darwin had spent some time in South America, his room on the ship was crowded with samples of the plants and animals he had collected.
ex.t: 达尔文在南美洲呆了一段时间后，他在船上的房间里挤满了他收集的动植物样本。

ex.s: They found the city too crowded.
ex.t: 他们觉得这座城市太拥挤。

ex.s: When the stadium is crowded.
ex.t: 当体育场拥挤时。

ex.s: Instead, as many as 800, 000 crowded the roads to the bridge.
ex.t: 多达80万人挤满了通往大桥的道路。

ex.s: The city was crowded with disappointed people with no interest in settling down, and when they heard there were new gold discoveries in Alaska, they left Dawson City as quickly as they had come.
ex.t: 这座城市挤满了失望的人们，他们无意定居，当听说阿拉斯加有新的金矿发现时，他们以当初来的速度离开了道森城。

defs.def: to fill your mind so that you can think of nothing else 涌上（心头）；涌入（脑海）
to stand very close to sb so that they feel uncomfortable or nervous 挤，靠近，挤在一旁（以致使人不舒服或紧张）
